newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * President Emil Constantinescu left for a two-day visit to Poland to meet his counterpart Aleksander Kwasniewski and boost bilateral ties and regional cooperation in the Central European Free Trade Association and the Black Sea Economic Cooperation.
Bucharest and Warsaw are not rivals in the race for NATO and EU admission, but will support each other, Constantinescu said ahead of his departure for Poland.
* Romanian Secretary of State Dumitru Ceausu and Ukrainian Deputy Foreign Minister Anton Buteiko resumed bilateral treaty talks in Bucharest on Monday.
Ceausu and Buteiko met Foreign Minister Adrian Severin during the morning.
Romania will advance a compromise package in order to reach an acceptable solution for both sides, ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said.
She said Romania wants to speed up negotiations frozen last year.
* Foreign Ministry Secretary of State Lazar Comanescu visited Turkey last week on mission to seek support for Romania's first-wave NATO integration bid.

* Constantinescu's personal involvement in fighting corruption is good, said Ion Diaconescu, leader of the National Peasant Party, backbone of the country's ruling coalition. He said miners leader Miron Cosma's arrest was normal.
* Gheorghe Funar, mayor of Transylvanian city of Cluj, called an extraordinary meeting of the city council to reject plans to set up a Hungarian consular office in Cluj.
* The upper Senate will meet in the afternoon for an extraordinary session during parliament recess. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
